resources.string: Find and fix problems in your game folders
Find broken disc sets, unfinished downloads and other library problems and fix them safely
Check your game folders for problems

Looks for empty or cut-off games, disc sets with missing tracks, leftovers of interrupted downloads and other things that stop games from working or only take space. Nothing changes until you pick a fix, and anything removed goes to Trash and recovery first.
The check was stopped. Nothing was changed.
The check could not finish. Make sure your game folders are reachable and try again.
Pick a download folder in Settings first, then check the library.
Some folders could not be read completely, so this list may be missing problems.
Only the first %1$d problems are shown. Fix some and check again to see the rest.
Only consoles this profile shows are checked. Shared folders are checked in the main profile.
These games will not start until they are fixed
Only takes space or clutters your frontend
There is no automatic fix for this. It is listed so you know about it.
Moves the files to Trash and recovery, where you can restore them.
Moves the old playlist to Trash and recovery and writes %1$s again with the discs that are still there:
Downloads %1$s again from the same source.
Moves this copy to Trash and recovery and downloads %1$s again from the same source.
Reads your game folders again so the library marks what is really on this device.
These files go to Trash and recovery. You can restore them there until the trash is emptied.
The files changed since the check. Check again first.
Could not fix %1$s. Anything already moved is in Trash and recovery.
%1$s may be in the wrong folder
Folder %1$s is not linked to a console
Library marks are out of date
This file is empty (0 bytes), so no emulator can start it. It was probably cut off while it was copied or downloaded.
This disc sheet lists track files that are not in its folder, so the game will not start.
This playlist names discs that are no longer in its folder. Rewrite it with the discs that are still there.
None of the discs this playlist names are in its folder. It only adds a broken entry to your frontend.
This disc sheet is empty or could not be read, so the game it describes may not start.
This file is %1$s, but the library lists it as %2$s. It was probably cut off; download it again for a complete copy.
No .cue or .gdi sheet in this folder lists these track files, so emulators cannot load them as a disc.
A download, unpack or copy that was interrupted left this temporary file behind. Nothing in the queue uses it.
This looks like a partial file from a browser or another download app. It cannot be played.
Several playlists in this folder list exactly the same discs, so the game shows up more than once.
This game has several discs but no .m3u playlist, so it shows once per disc and changing discs is harder.
This file type is for %1$s, but it is in the %2$s folder. Move it yourself if your frontend does not find it.
Game files on disk that are not marked yet: %1$d. Marked games that are no longer on disk: %2$d. A rescan brings the marks up to date.
